items.title: Simplify the menu to a buffet of local favorites
items.why: A focused buffet serves 40 guests well and cuts costs without compromising taste.

items.title: Swap a professional DJ for a curated playlist with a MC
items.why: A lively playlist plus a host keeps the party energetic at lower cost.

items.title: Use seasonal flowers and DIY balloon arches
items.why: Local blooms look fresh and DIY décor adds a personal touch.

items.title: Trim the contingency buffer slightly
items.why: A modest reduction frees a bit of cash while still covering unexpected needs.

answer.summary: Trim menus, entertainment and décor modestly, and shave the contingency to free enough cash without hurting the birthday vibe.

items.title: Scale back to a simple buffet
items.why: A modest menu satisfies 40 guests while cutting food costs.

items.title: Replace live band with a DJ
items.why: A DJ provides full‐party music at a lower price.

items.title: Use fewer floral arches and more fabric drapes
items.why: Keeps the venue festive yet cheaper than extensive flower setups.

items.title: Opt for a smaller tiered cake
items.why: Reduces cake cost while still offering a beautiful centerpiece.

answer.summary: Trim each major non‐essential category to its medium level, preserving the party vibe while freeing enough budget.

items.title: Switch to a reputable banquet hall caterer with set menu
items.why: A set menu for 250 guests trims per‐plate costs while keeping taste.

items.title: Opt for a DJ instead of a live band
items.why: A skilled DJ covers all ceremony and reception music for a large crowd.

items.title: Use seasonal marigold & rangoli instead of premium imports
items.why: Local flowers are vibrant in February and cut décor spend.

items.title: Limit extra priest assistants to essential rites
items.why: Core rituals stay sacred while auxiliary services are trimmed.

answer.summary: Replace high‐cost caterer and décor with local alternatives and trim extras to close the gap.

items.title: Trim contingency to essential buffers
items.why: Keeps a safety net while freeing most of the unused reserve.

items.title: Consolidate shuttles with fixed schedules
items.why: Reduces the number of vehicles without affecting guest comfort.

items.title: Simplify return‐gift packaging
items.why: Elegant yet modest packaging saves costs while still delighting guests.

answer.summary: Scale back the contingency, streamline transport, and modestly simplify gifts to bridge the shortfall.

items.title: Simplify flower arrangements
items.why: Local seasonal blooms look beautiful for a community pandal.

items.title: Scale back to essential audio‐visual
items.why: Core speeches and bhajans need clear sound, extra effects are optional.

items.title: Trim program to key performances
items.why: Focus on the most popular acts keeps the crowd engaged.

items.title: Lower contingency reserve
items.why: A modest buffer still protects against minor overruns.

answer.summary: Trim décor, audio‐visual, program and contingency to modest levels while preserving the event’s spirit.

items.title: Cut non‐essential permit fees
items.why: Basic civic permits suffice for a community event.

items.title: Scale back extra waste‐management services
items.why: Standard cleaning covers the venue for 400 guests.

items.title: Rely more on volunteer staff
items.why: Community volunteers can handle basic logistics without extra cost.

answer.summary: Trim minor permit, cleanup and volunteer logistics costs to bridge the small shortfall.
